analyzed_vuln.description: `SamsungV2Decompressor::decompressRow` performs unchecked neighbor reads from previously decoded rows when motion mode != 7. In the motion-prediction path it computes `refpixel = img_up2 + i + slideOffset` or `img_up + i + slideOffset + (...)` with `slideOffset` in {-4,-2,0,2,4} and then dereferences `*refpixel` (and sometimes `*(refpixel+2)`) without validating that the referenced column stays within row bounds. For left-edge blocks (`col==0`) and negative offsets, this can read before the start of the row buffer, producing ASan use-after-poison. Crash is observed in BitStream.h due to inlining, but root cause is this OOB reference-pixel access logic in `decompressRow`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: PoV routes through `SrwDecoder::decodeRawInternal` with compression 32773 (Samsung V2), allocates image data, then calls `SamsungV2Decompressor::decompress()`. Crafted compressed bitstream/header values drive `decompressRow<OptFlags::QP>` into a non-7 motion mode on rows >=2, so the predictor uses previous-row pointers with negative/shifted offsets near the first 16-pixel block. Because column boundary checks are missing, dereference of `refpixel`/`refpixel+2` hits poisoned redzone bytes adjacent to the image allocation and crashes.
